# CIRVYK implementation reference

This document describes CIRVYK's browser engine and bounded observation interface. The page at `#protocol` provides the reading layout; `#source` exposes reviewed public implementation files. Existing rule, schema, storage and deployment identifiers remain unchanged for compatibility; they are not the current brand name.

## 1. Deterministic processing

```
Sensor → Resistor → Capacitor → Comparator → Switch → Memory
```

`finalizeWindow({inputs, windowStart, now, coverage, parsingComplete, baseline, source, rules})` is pure. It normalizes the source and inputs, sorts inputs deterministically, filters them, derives the baseline and selects the result. It does not read clocks, network, DOM or storage itself.

The default `living-circuit.v1` rules are 60,000 milliseconds per UTC-aligned window, five preceding baseline windows, a minimum of ten accepted inputs for SURGE and a multiplier of two. Supported kinds are Activity and Transfer. The rule identifier is retained for compatibility; the CIRVYK rename does not change this contract.

The interval is `[start, end)`. The current time before `end` produces `accumulating`. An ended window with incomplete coverage, unresolved parsing or missing live scope produces `incomplete`. Only a final, complete window can produce QUIET, FLOW or SURGE. User-facing times use US Eastern (`America/New_York`) with automatic EDT/EST labels. Stored epochs, exported ISO timestamps and UTC-aligned processing windows remain unchanged.

For a final window:

- QUIET: zero accepted inputs.
- SURGE: all five consecutive preceding windows qualify, count ≥ 10, and count ≥ 2 × baseline average.
- FLOW: a non-empty final window that does not satisfy SURGE.

Baseline records must share the exact scope and rule configuration, be final with complete coverage and parsing, and occupy consecutive preceding intervals. A gap or conflicting count stops the baseline. Incomplete baseline gives null average and ratio. A zero complete baseline gives a null finite ratio; the count-based route condition still applies.

## 2. Input eligibility

Normalized input keys are `id, signature, mint, slot, timestamp, kind, source, address, accounts, verified, scopeId`.

Checks cover a valid integer UTC timestamp inside the selected interval, matching source mode, verified parser flag, supported kind and matching scope. A live input must also have the supported signature form, non-negative integer slot, target mint and configured observation accounts. It deduplicates by signature plus mint. An example requires a non-empty ID, deduplicates by that ID and cannot contain a claimed transaction signature.

Every rejected input remains inspectable as `{input, reason}`. These rules are bounded eligibility filtering rather than comprehensive anti-abuse detection.

## 3. Trace schema

Current schema: `circuit.trace.v1`, retained as the compatible record-format identifier.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| schema | Record format identifier |
| id | Stable scope/window/rules identity; not a cryptographic proof |
| window | start, end, durationMs, in UTC milliseconds |
| observedAt | The time passed into this engine invocation |
| source | mode, label, network, mint, accounts, scopeId |
| rulesVersion | Attached rule version |
| rules | version, windowMs, baselineWindows, surgeMinInputs, surgeMultiplier, supportedKinds |
| inputs | Normalized and sorted bounded input list |
| validInputs | Accepted inputs after eligibility and deduplication |
| filtered | Rejected input/reason pairs |
| count | validInputs.length |
| coverage | complete, partial or missing |
| parsingComplete | Boolean parsing condition supplied to the engine |
| baselineEvidence | Qualifying preceding-window identities, scope, count and completeness |
| baselineReady | Whether the required consecutive baseline is available |
| baselineAverage | Mean accepted baseline count or null |
| baselineReason | Baseline availability explanation |
| growthRatio | count / positive baselineAverage for a final window, else null |
| path | QUIET, FLOW, SURGE or null |
| status | accumulating, incomplete or final |
| reason | Pending-state explanation or null |
| progress | Window elapsed fraction, clamped to 0–1 |
| steps | Six id/name/label/inputCount/outputCount/status/detail records |

`validateTrace()` validates allowed shapes, reconstructs baseline evidence, reruns `finalizeWindow()` and compares every derived field with a stable representation. Imported JSON is data only.

## 4. Instrument semantics

`instruments.js` derives a read-only model from one selected Trace. It has no network calls, clock reads or random values.

- Relative activity uses input checks, filter checks, accepted Pulses, window evaluations, path selections and Trace preparations as explicit units. The final three are whole-window operations, not one operation per Pulse and not proof of a disk write.
- Each grid cell is an explicit interval labeled in US Eastern time, with EDT or EST selected for its timestamp. Its accepted count is a proven zero only when the Trace is final with complete coverage and parsing. In unknown coverage the model retains observed lower bounds separately and gives no completed bucket count.
- Waveform series are timestamped inputs and accepted inputs after filtering. They share an Eastern-time bucket axis and Pulse-per-bucket units; the underlying UTC-aligned buckets do not change. Equal curves are possible when no inputs were filtered; no random series is generated.
- Selecting a time subrange filters visible events and counts but does not recalculate the whole-window route or its baseline.
- Accepted final events can inspect all six stages. Rejected events stop at Sensor/Resistor; accepted incomplete events cannot claim a concluded Comparator/Switch/Memory path.

A file's declared `source.mode = live` is not proof of a current observation. The view positively distinguishes local observation, historical replay, imported claims and examples.

## 5. Read-only observation and coverage

One ObservationStore is shared across Home, Live, Core, Memory and the other pages. Page switching does not create another poller. It pauses periodic polling when hidden and keeps actual prior inputs/times on failure.

The Solana adapter checks finalized transactions involving explicitly configured accounts or pools, then inspects target-mint token balance or supported parsed SPL Token evidence. It is not an all-transactions index for a mint and does not classify an ordinary transfer as a buy or sell. Address membership is not beneficial ownership.

The current target is unconfigured because a new mint and explicit observed accounts were not supplied. CIRVYK is the configured brand. The X and GitHub links use the supplied project accounts; the token ticker, CA and trade link remain unconfigured. Optional RPC credentials stay server-side and are excluded from the public source set.

| State | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| unconfigured / invalid_configuration | Missing or invalid explicit scope; local examples remain available |
| ready / checking | Configuration loaded / shared request in progress |
| live + complete | Scan, finalized UTC boundary and parsing reconciled |
| live + partial | Only bounded/partial evidence or unresolved work is available |
| unavailable / error / rate_limited | Current proof is unavailable; retain previous successful evidence and timestamps |
| cursor_expired | Cursor changed scope or expired; restart once without it |

Only `[reconciledFrom,reconciledUntil)` is a proven range. Finalized slot and block time establish the upper boundary; unresolved parsing constrains it. Limits: four accounts, three pages × 50 signatures per account, 150 transactions per check, concurrency three, two retries, minimum 12-second request interval. Default browser polling is approximately 15 seconds; cursor memory is bounded to 100 entries and 30 minutes. Default retained browser inputs are 4,000. Pagination or retention limits are not exhaustive-history claims.

## 6. Local Workbench

Supported parameters are three patterns (1/12/6 inputs per batch), 60/120/300-second windows, one to five batches and 0.5×/1×/2×/4× playback speed. Automatic/manual replay, Execute, Pause, Step, Reset and Inspect result operate locally. Parameters rebuild the example record and device/waveform outputs through the actual engine. Reset retains the selected parameters. Live rules are unchanged.

The five preceding complete example windows each have three accepted inputs. Short burst with 60 seconds and one batch covers `2026-10-16T00:05:00Z` to `2026-10-16T00:06:00Z`: 12 received, 12 accepted, zero filtered; baseline average three, growth ratio four, SURGE. Fixture inputs have example provenance and no signatures.

The chassis and passive rails are display geometry. No remote worker registration, CPU allocation, burn activation, reward or transaction is part of Workbench execution.

## 7. Memory, provenance and public source

Memory keeps at most 30 records and 3 MB in the current browser, newest first. A stable window identity is updated rather than duplicated after late reconciliation. Quota or validation failures return explicit errors. JSON export includes the bounded inputs, rule configuration and baseline needed for replay; Snapshot is an actual downloadable PNG.

Imported historical chain declarations are not rechecked merely by importing them and do not enter locally observed live counts. Memory is not permanent, global, on-chain or collected while the page is closed.

Source generation uses an exact public path allowlist. It reads actual files, computes line/byte/file counts, rejects symlinks, oversized or credential-like material, and never walks the project to discover arbitrary files. Environment files, hosting metadata, server adapter and credentials are excluded. The browser presents content with text nodes, never HTML evaluation, and supports file switching, keyboard navigation, highlighting, copy and local scroll.

Wallet discovery uses Solana Wallet Standard registration and recognized injected Solana providers. The chooser displays OKX Wallet, Phantom, Backpack, Coinbase Wallet and Solflare, along with other compatible registered providers. Unavailable providers remain unavailable rather than simulated. A user-initiated connection supplies a public address for local filtering; the controller does not request signatures, transactions or token approvals. A matching address does not establish beneficial ownership or classify trading direction.

## 8. Shared operating context

Home provides the overview. Live inspects retained evidence. Core presents physical structure and processing; its compatibility route remains `#circuit`. Memory selects historical records. Source reads actual implementation. Workbench runs explicit local examples. Protocol is the technical manual.

The shared context identifies source and the selected range in US Eastern time. Component selection synchronizes circuit/activity/inspector. Grid selection synchronizes the visible time range, waveform and events. Event selection exposes its input and path. Saved Trace selection uses that record's data. `Clear filters` restores the full selection; `Live scope` exits replay; Home returns to the overview. Camera reset changes framing only.

# Self-hosted wallet and social marks

These assets identify third-party wallet providers and user-specified social destinations. Their presence does not imply partnership or endorsement. No third-party scripts, trackers, or remote image loads are used.

## Sources

- `public/assets/wallets/phantom.svg`: decoded icon from the [Solana wallet adapter Phantom adapter](https://github.com/anza-xyz/wallet-adapter/blob/master/packages/wallets/phantom/src/adapter.ts). Byte-identical to the already saved project reference asset.
- `public/assets/wallets/solflare.svg`: decoded icon from the [Solana wallet adapter Solflare adapter](https://github.com/anza-xyz/wallet-adapter/blob/master/packages/wallets/solflare/src/adapter.ts). Byte-identical to the already saved project reference asset.
- `public/assets/wallets/coinbase.svg`: decoded icon from the [Solana wallet adapter Coinbase adapter](https://github.com/anza-xyz/wallet-adapter/blob/master/packages/wallets/coinbase/src/adapter.ts).
- `public/assets/wallets/okx.png`: official [OKX Wallet website](https://web3.okx.com/) favicon, served at `https://web3.okx.com/cdn/assets/imgs/441/655A924890DB43CDA7E79F6A9CA93434.png`. Current 64×64 green checker symbol.
- `public/assets/wallets/backpack.png`: official [Backpack Wallet website](https://backpack.app/) icon, served at `https://backpack.app/icon/128x128.png`. 128×128 red backpack symbol.
- `public/assets/social-github.svg`: official Invertocat from [GitHub logo package](https://brand.github.com/GitHub_Logos.zip), `GitHub Logos/SVG/GitHub_Invertocat_White.svg`, geometry preserved and monochrome fill adapted to the site's muted header icon color. [Brand usage](https://brand.github.com/foundations/logo) permits a social button linking to a GitHub profile or project.
- `public/assets/social-x.svg`: existing reference implementation's X silhouette, preserved and self-hosted with the same muted header icon color.

## Scope

Logos are presentation assets only. Connection availability comes from actual Wallet Standard registration or recognized injected Solana provider detection. No wallet installation or asset custody is supplied by these images. The wallet names and logos remain trademarks of their respective owners.

01 / SYSTEM & INTERFACES

A market becomes a circuit.

CIRVYK turns a defined slice of token activity into bounded inputs, visible processing paths and replayable records. V1.1 restores the instrument around the V1 six-stage engine; it does not introduce a new consensus system or trading strategy.

The engine is a pure function of inputs, observation scope, epoch-aligned window, baseline and rules. Every page reads the same selected context. The Source workspace publishes the actual browser modules, configuration and documentation in an explicit public file set.

02 / SIX PROCESSING STAGES

One transaction, at most one Pulse.

A Pulse is a supported input admitted by the parser and the engine. A Trace describes one fixed processing window. A Snapshot is a PNG exported from a Trace. Multiple instructions in the same transaction do not multiply its Pulse count for the same target mint.

01 Sensor       normalize bounded inputs; preserve source and epoch timestamps
02 Resistor     verify eligibility; deduplicate; retain rejection reasons
03 Capacitor    accumulate accepted inputs inside [start, end)
04 Comparator   inspect the five preceding consecutive complete windows
05 Switch       select QUIET, FLOW or SURGE only for a final window
06 Memory       prepare the reproducible record for local persistence

Live inputs deduplicate by signature + mint; local fixtures deduplicate by input ID. Eligibility checks include time, source mode, parser verification, supported kind and scope. This is bounded filtering, not a complete anti-sybil or wash-trading detector.

The detailed SVG contains display structure as well as six interactive processing components. Passive traces, rails and framing are graphic topology. They do not claim independent online workers or additional processing stages.

03 / WINDOW & ROUTE RULES

Three paths. No hidden score.

QUIET

A reconciled, complete window contains zero valid inputs.

FLOW

The window contains valid inputs and does not meet the enhancement rule.

SURGE

At least 10 valid inputs and at least twice the mean of the preceding five complete consecutive windows.

Live observation uses 60-second epoch-aligned windows. Displayed times use US Eastern time (America/New_York), with automatic EDT/EST daylight-saving transitions. The start is inclusive and the end is exclusive. A baseline window must have the same scope and full rule configuration, be final, have complete coverage and complete parsing, and occupy its exact preceding position. A gap or conflicting count stops the consecutive baseline.

Engine stateConditionVisible conclusion
accumulatingThe current time is before window.endAccepted inputs may accumulate; path remains null
incompleteThe window ended but coverage, parsing or live scope is incompleteNo final path, including no QUIET conclusion
finalEnded window + complete coverage + complete parsing + configured scopeApply QUIET / FLOW / SURGE rules
Baseline unavailableFewer than five consecutive complete preceding windowsNo baseline average or growth ratio; non-empty final window is FLOW
Baseline average = 0All five qualifying baseline counts are zeroNo finite growth ratio; the count threshold still applies to route selection

Selecting a smaller time range filters the visible inputs and instruments. It does not recompute the whole-window route or invent a new baseline. The local Workbench can use 60, 120 or 300 seconds; this changes only its example Trace, not the live rule.

04 / TRACE FORMAT & MEMORY

Evidence travels with the trace.

The current record schema is circuit.trace.v1. These are actual fields returned by finalizeWindow(). Stored timestamps remain integer epoch milliseconds; the interface displays US Eastern time. Raw machine data and ISO strings retain their original instant; a missing derived value is null rather than a fabricated measurement.

FieldShape / meaning
schemaRecord format identifier: circuit.trace.v1
idDeterministic identity from scope, aligned start and full rules; an identity aid, not a cryptographic proof
window{ start, end, durationMs }; the processing interval [start, end)
observedAtTime passed to the engine for this record; not necessarily an input transaction time
source{ mode, label, network, mint, accounts, scopeId }; mode is live or example
rulesVersionThe rule version attached to this record
rules{ version, windowMs, baselineWindows, surgeMinInputs, surgeMultiplier, supportedKinds }
inputsNormalized, deterministically sorted bounded input list
validInputsInputs admitted after eligibility checks and deduplication
filteredRejected entries as { input, reason }, including duplicate decisions
countNumber of accepted inputs; equals validInputs.length
coveragecomplete, partial or missing for the processing record
parsingCompleteWhether parsing is complete for the supplied observation range
baselineEvidenceQualifying preceding records: id, window, source, rulesVersion, count, status, coverage and parsingComplete
baselineReadyTrue only when all five required preceding windows qualify
baselineAverageMean accepted count across the qualifying baseline, or null
baselineReasonExplanation of baseline availability and comparison
growthRatiocount / baselineAverage for a final record with a positive complete baseline; otherwise null
pathQUIET, FLOW, SURGE or null
statusaccumulating, incomplete or final
reasonPending-state explanation, or null for a final record
progressElapsed fraction of the window, bounded to [0, 1]
stepsSix records with id, name, label, inputCount, outputCount, status and detail

Input fields are limited to id, signature, mint, slot, timestamp, kind, source, address, accounts, verified, scopeId. The live reader emits Activity or Transfer when supported evidence is available. Local fixtures have no transaction signatures.

Memory is local to this browser: at most 30 records and 3 MB. The newest windows are retained first; an updated record replaces the same fixed-window ID. JSON exports contain the inputs, baseline evidence and rule configuration. Import validates the data shape, reruns the actual engine, and compares every derived field before saving.

An imported file can declare live provenance, but that declaration is not a fresh chain verification. Imported historical records stay outside locally observed live counts and use historical labeling. A Snapshot is a downloadable PNG, not a public record link, a permanent shared memory or an on-chain write.

05 / OBSERVATION & COVERAGE

Observed does not mean everything.

The read-only Solana adapter queries explicitly configured accounts or pools, then examines finalized transactions for target-mint token balance changes or supported parsed SPL Token operations. A mint address alone does not index all token activity. Plain transfers are never relabeled as buys or sells, and an account-list match does not establish beneficial ownership.

Reader / coverage stateMeaningWhat the instrument does
unconfigured / invalid_configurationA required scope value is absent or invalidShow configuration scope; local examples and saved replay remain usable
ready / checkingConfiguration loaded / one shared request in progressRetain source labels, previous values and their timestamps
live + completeAccount scan, finalized timestamp boundary and transaction parsing reconciledFinalize only ended windows fully inside the proven interval
live + partialBounded pagination, pending parsing or only part of the range is provenExpose retained inputs and unresolved reasons; do not infer empty coverage
unavailable / error / rate_limitedA valid range cannot currently be establishedKeep the previous successful inputs and actual timestamps; allow another check
cursor_expiredThe bounded server cursor expired or changed scopeRestart once without that cursor; deduplicate the returned evidence

Only [reconciledFrom, reconciledUntil) is a proven range. Finalized slot and block time establish its upper boundary. Unresolved transactions constrain that boundary. Pagination limits and retention cutoffs cannot be presented as an exhaustive token history.

All seven pages share one reader. It checks approximately every 15 seconds while the page is open and visible; hidden-page polling pauses. Limits are four observed accounts, three pages of 50 signatures per account, 150 transactions per check, concurrency three and at most two retries. Cursor storage is bounded to 100 entries with a 30-minute lifetime. The interface keeps at most 4,000 retained input records by default.

A connected wallet supplies a public-address filter over observed account relationships. It requests no signature, approval, transaction or custody. Pasting a public address provides the same filtering purpose.

06 / OPERATING THE INSTRUMENT

One selection, across the panels.

  1. Choose a context. The shared context strip identifies local example, live scope or historical replay, with its actual window in US Eastern time. Load example opens an explicit fixture. Live scope exits replay and returns to the scoped reader.
  2. Inspect a component. Hover to preview, click to retain the selection. The circuit, relative activity display and inspector use the same selected stage. Drag or zoom the circuit; Reset view restores its framing.
  3. Select a time range. Each activity-grid cell has an explicit Eastern time interval and accepted count. Selecting a cell narrows the related input list and highlights the same waveform bins. Unknown coverage is not colored as a proven zero.
  4. Inspect an event. Open its input evidence and filter reason, then locate its processing path. Accepted final inputs pass through six stages; rejected inputs stop at the filter. An incomplete window can inspect accumulation but cannot replay a concluded route.
  5. Replay a saved Trace. Choose it in Memory. The selected context and related instruments switch to that record and retain the historical timestamp. Playback does not add live events.
  6. Recover the full view. Clear filters removes time, event and component filters. Live scope leaves replay; Home returns to the overview. Resetting the circuit view changes only framing, not data or counts.

Local Workbench procedure

Choose Single pulse, Short burst or Gradual flow. Set a 60-, 120- or 300-second example window and one to five input batches. The default batch contains respectively 1, 12 or 6 inputs; the maximum is 60 inputs. Each example carries five fixed preceding baseline windows with three accepted inputs each.

Parameter changes rebuild the example Trace, chassis readouts, waveform and output through the same engine. Execute local inputs advances the six stages; Pause retains the current step, Step inspects one stage, and Reset rewinds playback while retaining the selected parameters. Automatic or manual mode changes how the path advances. Speed choices of 0.5×, 1×, 2× and 4× affect playback timing only.

The Workbench is browser-local. Its restored chassis is a display model. No remote worker is registered, no CPU capacity is rented, no token is burned and no transaction is sent.

07 / WORKED EXAMPLE

Twelve inputs, one inspectable route.

Use Short burst, a 60-second window and one batch in the Workbench. The fixture covers 2026-10-15 20:05:00–20:06:00 EDT (UTC-04:00). All 12 local Activity inputs occur inside the window, have unique IDs, and carry example provenance without signatures.

The activity graph shows the burst's timestamped inputs; the accepted series matches it because nothing was filtered. Comparator, Switch and Memory each perform one whole-window evaluation in the relative activity display. These are different units, not a temperature scale or six identical Pulse counters.

08 / QUESTIONS & REFERENCES

Read the mechanism, then inspect it.

Does SURGE mean buy or sell?
No. It is the result of a deterministic display rule over an observed count, not a forecast or valuation.
Why is an empty-looking circuit sometimes pending?
Missing evidence is different from a reconciled empty window. QUIET requires complete coverage, complete parsing and an ended window.
What works before a target is configured?
Local Workbench, full component inspection, the public Source workspace, saved-record import/export, replay and PNG Snapshot export. Live target observation needs a new mint and at least one explicit account or pool.
Does the system continue collecting when the page closes?
No. This version checks while open and visible. Memory persists only in this browser until records or browser storage are removed.
Can importing JSON prove an on-chain event?
No. The engine can verify internal consistency. Independent chain provenance requires a successful read through the configured observation scope.

# CIRVYK

![CIRVYK cube logo, wordmark and circuit artwork captured from the application](docs/media/cirvyk-header.jpg)

**A circuit that remembers.**

CIRVYK is a circuit-based interface for observing a defined slice of Solana token activity. It represents incoming events as signals moving through visible processing stages, connecting individual inputs to changes in circuit state.

Inspect a component, follow a signal through its path, and revisit the Trace produced by a processing window.

[Website](https://www.cirvyk.xyz/#home) · [Protocol](docs/protocol.md) · [Development](docs/development.md)

## Overview

The reader checks finalized transactions involving explicitly configured Solana accounts and looks for evidence concerning a target mint. A shared browser store feeds those inputs into a deterministic engine. Circuit components, instruments and event details expose the same selected result.

This repository contains the complete application: native browser ES modules, HTML, CSS, SVG artwork, the Node observation API, tests, configuration and documentation. No frontend framework or bundle compiler is required. Without live configuration, the interface starts with explicitly labeled, reproducible local examples.

![CIRVYK overview showing the circuit, activity field, time grid and input ledger](docs/media/cirvyk-overview.jpg)

*Local example inputs, not current chain activity. Displayed dates and times use US Eastern time.*

## Interface

| View | Purpose | Main interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Shared system overview | Select a component or processing interval |
| Live | Scoped input inspection | Filter events and inspect their evidence |
| Core | Circuit structure and stage details | Pan, zoom, select a component and replay a path |
| Memory | Browser-local Trace history | Save, reopen, import or export a record |
| Source | Actual reviewed public files | Browse files, inspect code and copy content |
| Workbench | Local signal laboratory | Change example parameters and execute or step through stages |
| Protocol | Technical manual | Read rules, responsibilities and data boundaries |

Core retains the `#circuit` route. Source remains an internal reader; the header GitHub icon opens this repository separately.

## Signal processing

```text
Observe → Filter → Accumulate → Compare → Route → Record
```

| Component | Implemented responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sensor | Normalize and order supplied inputs |
| Resistor | Check eligibility and retain rejection reasons |
| Capacitor | Accumulate accepted inputs in one window |
| Comparator | Evaluate preceding complete-window evidence |
| Switch | Choose QUIET, FLOW or SURGE from the result |
| Memory | Prepare the inspectable record and replay evidence |

These stages belong to `finalizeWindow()` in [engine.js](public/modules/engine.js). Their visual components are not independent services or AI agents.

Live event identity is `signature:mint`; example identity is a non-empty input ID. Duplicate inputs are filtered. Default windows span 60 seconds, include their start and exclude their end. A baseline requires five consecutive preceding complete windows with matching scope and rules.

A final empty window selects QUIET. SURGE requires at least ten accepted inputs and at least twice the baseline average; other non-empty final windows select FLOW. Accumulating or incomplete windows have no final path. Missing coverage is not treated as a verified zero. Thresholds are defined in [rules.js](public/config/rules.js).

## Traces and replay

A `circuit.trace.v1` record retains normalized inputs, filtering results, source identity, window bounds, exact rules, baseline evidence, stage outputs and the selected path. Import validation reruns the engine and compares the result. Reproduction depends on the saved rules and baseline, not just the final count.

Memory uses browser local storage, with limits of 30 records and 3 MiB. JSON import/export preserves the record; PNG Snapshot exports its visual summary. Historical and example contexts stay distinct from current local observation. Replay does not add live inputs or establish independent chain provenance.

## Getting started

Use Node.js 22 or 24 and pnpm 10.28.0. The repository pins pnpm and includes its lockfile.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/theovarne/CIRVYK.git
cd CIRVYK
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm build
pnpm dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5175`. `pnpm dev` serves `public/` and both API routes on loopback. `pnpm test` runs the existing Node test suites. `pnpm build` validates reviewed file hashes, configuration and the generated Source manifest; it does not compile assets. The committed `public/` files are the frontend output, while observation also requires the API source.

For a reproducible example, open Workbench and choose Short burst, a 60-second window and one batch: twelve inputs, zero filtered, baseline average three and SURGE. Execute, inspect a stage, save the Trace and reopen it in Memory.

## Configuration

Examples need no credentials. Live observation requires a server-side target and explicit accounts.

| Setting | Requirement and scope |
| --- | --- |
| `CIRCUIT_MINT` | Required for live mode; public target mint |
| `CIRCUIT_OBSERVED_ACCOUNTS` | Required for live mode; up to four public accounts, separated by commas or whitespace |
| `CIRCUIT_NETWORK` | Optional; `mainnet-beta` by default, also `devnet` or `testnet` |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL` | Optional, server-only HTTPS provider override |
| `SOLANA_RPC_API_KEY` | Optional, server-only bearer credential |
| `PORT` | Optional local server port; default `5175` |

[.env.example](.env.example) contains empty configuration fields. The server does not automatically load `.env`; export values or explicitly run `node --env-file=.env scripts/dev.mjs`. Keep real credentials outside Git. `/api/config` exposes the observation scope while omitting the provider URL and key.

Public identity and project links live in [site.js](public/config/site.js). Changing website branding does not rename compatible schemas, storage keys or routes.

## Data and execution boundaries

Observation is bounded to configured accounts and parser-supported Activity/Transfer evidence, not complete market coverage or buy/sell classification. One shared reader checks approximately every fifteen seconds while the browser is visible. It pauses when hidden; closing the browser stops collection. There is no backend Trace database.

Wallet Standard and recognized Solana extensions supply a public address only after user approval. That address filters already observed relationships; it does not prove ownership or trading direction. CIRVYK reads activity and exposes processing state. It does not execute trades or request token approvals.

Human-readable time uses `America/New_York`, selecting EDT or EST for each timestamp. Stored epochs, ISO exchange fields and UTC-aligned processing boundaries remain stable for replay compatibility.
